st.headline: 80% of companies in SCCCI survey flag rising costs as top concern amid global uncertainty
st.teaser: The Government is moving to ease regulatory burdens for SMEs.
fullText: SINGAPORE – Rising business costs have become a bigger concern for companies in Singapore amid global uncertainty caused by the conflict in the Middle East.
But the Government is moving to ease regulatory burdens for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), as more firms expect lower profits in 2026.

A Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCCI) survey of 540 local businesses found that 80 per cent of respondents were concerned about rising business costs, up from 65 per cent a year earlier.
Market uncertainty, weaker demand and supply chain disruptions were also among the top challenges cited, amid global uncertainty stemming from the Iran war.
Businesses were also concerned about the availability of suitable manpower, as well as the need to transform and pivot towards new growth areas.
Against that backdrop, 78 per cent of respondents expect to remain profitable in 2026, although 56 per cen t expect lower profits than in 2025.

To cope with the challenging environment, businesses said they were absorbing higher costs to maintain customer relationships, passing on some cost increases to customers and cutting costs , as well as diversifying into new markets.
The poll, which was conducted from May to July, also found that businesses are taking tentative steps towards adopting artificial intelligence.

Some 45 per cent of respondents said they were experimenting with off-the-shelf AI tools as a first step towards broader integration. The biggest hurdles were uncertainty over how to adopt AI comprehensively rather than in a piecemeal way, a lack of in-house expertise and the cost of implementation.
On internationalisation, Malaysia was the top overseas market of interest, followed by Indonesia, China, Vietnam and Thailand.

Businesses also said they were looking to South-east Asia to tap the region’s growth potential, strengthen sourcing and procurement of goods and materials, and expand their manufacturing and production capabilities.
At the annual Small and Medium Enterprises and Infocomm Commerce Conferen ce on Aug 5, SCCCI president Kho Choon Keng announced the formation of an international advisory panel.

“Through the (panel), SCCCI seeks to provide our members and Singapore businesses with strategic guidance and distinctive insights on geopolitical, economic and market developments, while fostering new partnerships and cross-border collaboration involving businesses in Singapore, South-east Asia, China and beyond,” Kho said.

Speaking at the event held at Suntec Singapore Convention and Exhibition Centre, Minister for National Development Chee Hong Tat said the Government would improve regulatory efficiency and reduce compliance burdens, particularly for SMEs.

Chee announced two upcoming measures to streamline approvals for businesses, as part of the work of the Inter-Ministerial Committe e on Pro-Enterprise Rules Review, which was launched in 2024 and is chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong.

Medical clinic operators in commercial buildings currently need approval from both the Ministry of Health (MOH) and the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA), unless the building’s total clinic space does not exceed 1,000 sq m.

Chee said that these operators will not need to submit a change-of-use application to URA if they have obtained MOH’s prior approval and the building’s total clinic space does not exceed 3,000 sq m or 20 per cent of its total commercial gross floor area, whichever is lower.
Meanwhile, businesses within the Changi Airport development will not need to seek separate approval from URA when switching between commercial uses, such as converting a shop into a restaurant.

URA will instead authorise such uses upfront within approved commercial units, as well as childcare centres and community building uses, subject to conditions including prior approval from the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore.
URA will provide more details later in 2026 when it implements both changes.
Chee said: “This means that an applicant in either situation can save $500 and two weeks of waiting time for each application.
“Both these measures will reduce the double handling... It’s a lose-lose situation if we have too many of these unnecessary red tape in the system.”
Beyond these specific measures, Chee said the Government wants to encourage “a pro-business approach” across agencies by streamlining administrative processes to save time, money and manpower.
He added that the Government would continue working with businesses to tackle challenges posed by AI, climate change and technological change.

For example, government agencies will continue to work with labour unions and government partners – including trade associations like the SCCCI – to businesses in Singapore to help them build digital capabilities, access AI tools and upskill their workforce.
Businesses also need to carefully assess their vulnerability to climate risks and consider measures to ensure business continuity under more extreme climate conditions.

Chee said : “As more investors use climate-related disclosures to understand companies’ environmental strategies and to inform their investment decisions, businesses also have to build their capabilities in areas such as sustainability solutions and reporting.

“We welcome more businesses to tap the Sustainability Reporting Grant by Enterprise Singapore and the Economic Devlopment Board to strengthen your sustainability capabilities and to better position your company for a low-carbon economy.”
He also encouraged SMEs to tap SME Centres, which provide a wide range of support, including business advisory, to facilitate the adoption and implementation of AI solutions.

“At a time when the global environment is increasingly uncertain and challenging, businesses, including our SME community, need to look beyond established playbooks to plan their strategies,” he said.

cna.headline: Primary 1 registration: Nearly half of all primary schools oversubscribed in Phase 2C
cna.teaser: Phase 2C is open to all students and is usually the most competitive. Use CNA's interactive table to find the results for every primary school.
fullText: Phase 2C is considered the most competitive phase and is open to all children. Forty places in each primary school are reserved for this phase.
Use our table to find the results for every primary school:
This was followed by Northland Primary School in Yishun, which drew 141 applicants for 42 places.
Nan Hua Primary School, Chongfu School and Rosyth School completed the top five.
Princess Elizabeth, Northland, Nan Hua and Chongfu were also among the top five last year.
Registration for this phase opened at 9am Jul 28 and closed at 4.30pm on Jul 30.
In most cases, balloting is conducted when the number of applicants exceeds the number of vacancies. It takes place in any phase from Phase 2A to Phase 2C supplementary.

Priority admission into the school is given in this order: Singaporeans living within 1km of the school, Singaporeans living between 1km and 2km of the school, followed by Singaporeans living further than 2km from the school. Next come permanent residents in the same distance groups.

The next phase, 2C supplementary, is for children who have yet to be registered in a primary school.
The vacancies for the next phase will be updated by 1pm on Aug 11.
MOE cut the Primary 1 intake for most schools earlier this year in view of significantly falling student cohort sizes in 2027 and the coming years.
At the time, the ministry said the cuts would minimise the need for school mergers or relocations and maintain a good geographical spread of primary schools for students across Singapore.
Compared to 2025, there are 1,460 fewer spots overall in 2026. Of the 179 primary schools in Singapore, 61 cut their intake while 12 schools increased the number of spaces available.

listening.title: Singapore's Electric Bus Transition Gets Green Light
listening.transcript: Singapore is accelerating its transition to a cleaner public transport system by deploying more electric buses on the road. The Land Transport Authority aims to have a hundred percent clean energy bus fleet by twenty-forty. Commuters will enjoy quieter rides and reduced carbon emissions, though the infrastructure roll-out requires massive power grid upgrades. This green transition represents a significant milestone in Singapore's climate action plan.

economistArticle.title: Efficiency Over Excess: Why China’s AI Models Punch Above Their Weight
paras: Silicon Valley’s recipe for artificial intelligence has long been one of brute force: pour in billions of dollars, buy up hundreds of thousands of Nvidia’s top-tier chips, and build massive data centres that consume as much electricity as small cities. This high-octane approach has allowed American tech giants to maintain a commanding lead in pure computational capacity. Yet, beneath this mountain of cash lies an uncomfortable truth: the marginal utility of throwing capital at AI may be starting to diminish.

Meanwhile, across the Pacific, Chinese tech firms and researchers are operating under strict constraints. Denied access to America’s most advanced semiconductors and working with a fraction of the venture capital funding, Chinese engineers have had no choice but to innovate through necessity. Instead of relying on sheer computing power, they have focused heavily on algorithmic efficiency, fine-tuning smaller models, and optimizing software to wring every drop of performance out of older hardware.

The results are striking. While American models like GPT-4 require astronomical resources to run, Chinese equivalents developed by firms like DeepSeek and Baidu are achieving comparable benchmarks at a mere fraction of the cost. By refining data curation, utilising mixture-of-experts architectures, and squeezing efficiencies out of open-source frameworks, Chinese developers have demonstrated that ingenuity can often bypass financial deficits. They are, in essence, getting much better bang for their buck.

This divergence in strategy highlights a fundamental cultural shift in technology development. In the West, AI development is treated as a frontier exploration where scale is king. In China, it is increasingly treated as an engineering optimization problem, where frugality and targeted application are the priorities. This pragmatic ethos is highly suited to commercial deployment, where businesses care far more about cost-per-query than they do about theoretical benchmarks.

To be sure, America’s raw spending power and access to state-of-the-art silicon still give it an edge in pioneering next-generation architectures. But as the AI race transitions from experimental breakthroughs to practical, widespread adoption, the victors may not be those who spend the most, but those who waste the least. China’s hyper-efficient approach serves as a timely reminder that in the realm of technology, constraints can sometimes be a catalyst for unparalleled cleverness.
economistArticle.cn:
硅谷发展人工智能的秘诀长期以来一直是一种“蛮力”模式：注入数十亿美元资金，买下成千上万张英伟达的顶级芯片，并建造消耗相当于小城市电力的庞大数据中心。这种高消耗的方法使美国科技巨头在纯计算能力上保持了绝对领先。然而，在这座金山之下却隐藏着一个令人不安的事实：向人工智能砸钱的边际效用可能已经开始递减。
与此同时，在大洋彼岸，中国科技公司和研究人员正在严格的限制下运营。由于无法获得美国最先进的半导体，且仅拥有西方风险资金的一小部分，中国工程师别无选择，只能迫于无奈进行创新。他们没有依赖庞大的计算能力，而是高度专注于算法效率、微调较小的模型以及优化软件，以从较旧的硬件中榨干每一滴性能。
其结果令人瞩目。虽然像 GPT-4 这样的美国模型需要天文数字般的资源才能运行，但像 DeepSeek 和百度等公司开发出的中国同等模型，却仅以极小部分的成本实现了不相上下的基准表现。通过精细化数据清洗、利用混合专家（MoE）架构，并从开源框架中挤出效率，中国开发者证明了创造力往往可以弥补资金赤字。实质上，他们获得了更高的性价比。
这种策略上的分歧凸显了技术发展中根本性的文化转变。在西方，AI 研发被视为一场“规模至上”的开拓性探索。在中国，它正日益被视为一个工程优化问题，其中节俭和针对性应用才是首要任务。这种务实的风气非常适合商业部署，因为企业对“单次查询成本”的关心远胜于对理论基准的关心。
诚然，美国庞大的资金实力和获取最先进芯片的渠道，使其在开拓下一代架构方面仍占有优势。但随着 AI 竞争从实验性突破转向实际、广泛的应用，最终的胜者可能不是花钱最多的人，而是浪费最少的人。中国超高效的研发路径适时地提醒了我们：在技术领域，限制有时反而是激发出无与伦比智慧的催化剂。

gems.s: Yet, beneath this mountain of cash lies an uncomfortable truth: the marginal utility of throwing capital at AI may be starting to diminish.
gems.why: This sentence uses an inverted structure ('beneath this mountain... lies...') to build dramatic tension before introducing the main point, followed by a colon for a clean, logical revelation. 这个句子采用了倒装句式（'beneath this mountain... lies...'）来营造戏剧张力，随后使用冒号进行了干净、逻辑性强的揭示。

gems.s: But as the AI race transitions from experimental breakthroughs to practical, widespread adoption, the victors may not be those who spend the most, but those who waste the least.
gems.why: This sentence employs antithesis ('not be those who spend... but those who waste...') to create a memorable, balanced comparison that challenges standard industry beliefs. 这个句子运用了对仗手法（'不是那些花钱最多的人，而是那些浪费最少的人'），创造出了令人印象深刻、富有平衡感的对比，从而挑战了行业传统观念。
